items.name: First screen
items.reason: From the headline, the decision block and the frontier claim, a reader knows the lean (Brisk-S, low reasoning, 1 retry), why it is the lean (it is the knee, and above it no single step is separated), and what is unresolved: no floor or price per point was declared. The top option's +1.5 points at about 12 times the cost is stated up front. Watch names multi-hop questions and the unbudgeted 513 ms p95.

items.name: Coherent story
items.reason: Every block's rows match their sentences. Claim prices rises step by step from $3.20 to $17,236.36. In claim below, J and S differ by 2.6, 2.1, 2.3 and 2.2 points across the four tasks. Claim tasks has multi-hop lowest in all three columns. The tool's price frontier holds 7 options, so the 'seven' is right. But claim below and the lede call Nano-XS high reasoning 1 retry (S, $0.111) 'the nearest cheaper option'. Claim retry's own block shows Brisk-S low reasoning no retry (I) at $0.288: cheaper than the lean by only $56 a month, and 1.9 points behind (+0.3 to +3.4). The page contradicts itself about what sits just below the lean.

items.name: Honest emphasis
items.reason: The lean's weak axes are visible: multi-hop, latency, and no budget. Above the lean, the unseparated +0.8 steps are not oversold. But the best-of-eighteen caveat and Watch put the lean's thinnest lead below it at +0.8 (the low end against S). The real thinnest lead is against I, whose low end is +0.3 (compare.brisk-s.low.r1.brisk-s.low.r0.pass_rate.overall.interval). So the margin the lean's place rests on reads stronger than it is. 'Never down' in the pairing caveat is also stated more firmly than an assumption about pairing supports.

items.name: Sound elision
items.reason: No omitted item would change the call. The off-frontier options are all dearer and weaker than a frontier option. The retry, reasoning and calls-per-task items agree with the shown claims. Outcome and extra calls have no figures. One small error: the 'off the frontier' note says each left-out option costs more than one that passes as many. That does not fit I, which is off only the price curve, not dominated.

items.name: Confounds handled
items.reason: The unpaired design is carried into the caveats and into a paired re-run. Method admits the snapshot does not say what the 4,000,000-a-month volume counts. Cost is per 1,000 calls, and calls per task run from 1.43 to 1.89 across options. If the volume counts tasks, every monthly figure and the $319.67 to $1,595.18 band shift by roughly half. That never reaches the confidence line or the decision block, where the owner is asked to price a point in those dollars.

items.name: Actionable next steps
items.reason: Each step names a declaration or an experiment and what it settles. The 6,044 cases per arm to tell the lean from Atlas-M low reasoning 1 retry four times in five checks out (settle.brisk-s.low.r1.atlas-m.low.r1.pass_rate.overall.cases_needed_80). The multi-hop step is looser but says what it would show.

items.name: Evidence fits claims
items.reason: Each claim's figure is in its block, and the counterfactual holds: if the J-vs-S or J-vs-F gaps flipped, claims below and above would have to change. Captions describe what is drawn. One weakness: the first block in claim above shows the model rows as Atlas-M to Brisk-S (-0.8, -0.7), while its sentence talks about Atlas-M's gain. The reader has to flip the signs.

findings.finding: Claim below, the lede ('the nearest by 2.4 points') and the best-of-eighteen caveat all treat Nano-XS high reasoning 1 retry (S) as the nearest cheaper option. Brisk-S low reasoning no retry (I) is cheaper than the lean by only $56 a month ($0.288 vs $0.302 per 1k calls). It trails by just +1.9 points (+0.3 to +3.4), which is the lean's thinnest separated lead, and claim retry already shows it. Fix: either call S the nearest cheaper option on the price frontier and say I sits between them off that frontier, or name I as the nearest cheaper option. Then rebase the best-of-eighteen caveat and Watch on the +0.3 low end against I. A fresh run that reads the lean about 0.3 points lower, or more, leaves no separated gain over I, and I is $56 a month cheaper.

The price band ($319.67 to $1,595.18 a month per point) and the monthly costs assume the 4,000,000 volume counts the same calls that cost per 1k is priced on. Method says the snapshot does not say what the volume counts, and calls per task differ by option (1.45 to 1.57 among the frontier options above Nano-XS low reasoning). Carry this into the 'Where the answer flips' line or the 'Nothing declares' caveat. Also say whether the lean stays the knee if cost is read per task: on point figures it does, but the band rises by about half.

The first block in claim above draws the model effect as Atlas-M to Brisk-S (-0.8, -2.0 to +0.5; -0.7, -1.7 to +0.4). The sentence describes Atlas-M's gain over the lean. Flip the rows to Brisk-S to Atlas-M (+0.8, +0.7) so the bars point the way the sentence reads.

The pairing caveat says pairing 'can only narrow' the intervals and would move the lean up 'never down'. Pairing narrows intervals only if outcomes are positively correlated across shared cases. Soften this to 'would likely narrow'. Also note that the best-of-eighteen caveat can move the estimate the other way.

The 'Left out' note says every option off the frontier costs more than one that passes at least as many tasks. That is untrue for Brisk-S low reasoning no retry (I), which is off only the price curve. Reword the note, or name I as the exception.

items.name: First screen
items.reason: The headline, lede and decision block say what to do and why. The lean is Brisk-S with low reasoning and one retry, the knee of the price curve. The top option passes +1.5 points (+0.3 to +2.6) more at about 12 times the cost. The nearest cheaper option, Brisk-S with low reasoning and no retry, saves $56 a month and trails by +1.9 (+0.3 to +3.4). Nothing was declared, so the decider sets the price. The main risk sits in Watch: that thin lead, the weak multi-hop task and a 513 ms p95 with no budget to read it against. The frontier claim backs this up.

items.name: Coherent story
items.reason: The claims agree with their blocks row by row. In the prices claim each step costs more per point than the last: $3.20, $17.31, $111.22, $319.67, $1,595.18 and $17,236.36, which matches the price_tradeoff output. In the above claim none of the single steps over the lean is separated (+0.8, -0.4 to +2.1, and Atlas-M with low reasoning ahead by +0.8, -2.0 to +0.5 read the other way). Only the top option is separated, at +1.5. The below claim's +1.9 and +2.4 match their blocks. In the retry claim, gains rise as the starting pass rate falls (+0.9, +1.9, +7.5). The latency claim rises with cost (450 to 2551 ms). Last round's must_fix is resolved: the below claim, the lede, the pick-of-many caveat and Watch now name the no-retry option as the nearest cheaper option.

items.name: Honest emphasis
items.reason: The lean's weak axes are on the page: its thinnest separated lead (low end +0.3, and a fresh run of today's size reads it the other way 0.8% of the time, as settle_cases confirms), multi-hop as its weakest task at 95.6%, and its p95 of 513 ms. The pairing caveat now says pairing 'would likely narrow' the intervals, and it notes that the pick-of-many effect pulls the other way. The price band is labelled as point prices with no interval.

items.name: Sound elision
items.reason: None of the left-out items would change the call. Last round's issue with the 'Left out' note is fixed: it now names Brisk-S with low reasoning and no retry as off only the price curve. The off-frontier options, the other retry and reasoning effects, and the per-task rates without counts are all in the appendix or covered by the claims.

items.name: Confounds handled
items.reason: All three caveats code lists (no control, nothing declared, pick of eighteen) are carried with what would make each material. The volume-unit confound raised last round now has its own caveat. It gives the calls-per-task range (1.452 to 1.566) and says the band rises by about half while the knee holds. My own per-task arithmetic agrees. Unpaired intervals are named in every block.

items.name: Actionable next steps
items.reason: Each next step names an experiment or a declaration and what it would settle. The 6,044 cases per arm for the comparison with Atlas-M with low reasoning matches settle_cases. But the paired re-run leaves out Brisk-S with low reasoning and no retry. That is the comparison Watch and the pick-of-many caveat call the lean's thinnest separated lead, and the reason the cheaper option could be the better buy. No next step tests it directly.

items.name: Evidence fits claims
items.reason: Most blocks fit their claims, and the caption on the model rows in the above claim now explains the sign, which resolves last round's direction finding. Three blocks fit less well. The retry claim says a retry is 'the cheapest lift on every model' and quotes $24 a month, but its block draws only pass-rate changes with no cost. The frontier claim says 'a frontier of seven options', but its block marks only the lean, so a reader can't see which seven. The no-retry option is undominated, which makes eight on a dominance reading. The tasks claim says 'on either side of it', but the block shows the top option, not Brisk-S with high reasoning and one retry, the frontier step just above the lean.

findings.finding: Add Brisk-S with low reasoning and no retry to the paired re-run in Next steps. Watch and the pick-of-many caveat both name the lean's lead over it (+1.9, +0.3 to +3.4) as the thinnest, and that is where the $56-a-month cheaper option could become the better buy. Today's design needs about 1,636 cases per arm to separate them four times in five when read unpaired (settle_cases); pairing needs fewer. Say that this re-run settles whether the lean's lead survives on fresh cases.

'A frontier of seven options' counts the price curve, which is how price_tradeoff counts it. But Brisk-S with low reasoning and no retry ($0.288, 95.3%) is undominated, and the page calls it 'off only the price curve'. Say 'price curve' in the claim, and mark the seven curve options in the scatter so the block shows the frontier the sentence names.

The claim says a retry is 'the cheapest lift on every model' and quotes $24 a month for Nano-XS with reasoning off, but the block shows only pass-rate changes. Add each retry step's monthly cost gap, or its price per point, beside the rows, or cut 'cheapest' from the sentence. Also note that a retry raises calls per task (1.698 to 1.888 on Nano-XS with reasoning off), so the $24 grows if the volume counts tasks.

'The frontier options on either side of it' implies the next step up, Brisk-S with high reasoning and one retry, but the heatmap shows the top option, Atlas-M with high reasoning and one retry. Either swap in Brisk-S with high reasoning and one retry, whose weakest task is also multi-hop at 97.3%, or reword to 'the frontier option below it and the top option'.
